Surah "Al-Zalzalah" (The Earthquake)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿When the earth is shaken with its (final) shaking﴾. That is: it is set in motion, its violent shaking, after which there will be no (other) shaking. It is also recited with a fatha on the zay, so the kasra form (zilzal) is a verbal noun (masdar), and the fatha form (zalzal) is a noun (ism).

﴿And the earth will bring forth its burdens﴾: i.e., its treasures and its dead, the plural of "thiql" (ثِقْل), which is the goods of a household. What is within its belly of hidden treasures has been made into its burdens.

And man will say, "What is wrong with it?" — it has been shaken with its violent shaking, and has cast out what is in its belly! This is at the second blast, when it is shaken and casts out its dead alive. So they will say this because of the dreadful matter that appears to them, just as they say: ﴿Who has raised us up from our sleeping-place?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 52]. It was also said: this is the words of the disbeliever, because he did not believe in resurrection. As for the believer, he will say: ﴿This is what the Most Merciful promised, and the messengers spoke truly﴾ [Ya-Sin: 52].

"On that Day" (﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾) is a substitute (badal) for "when" (إذا) in the preceding phrase, and the verb governing it is ﴿تُحَدِّثُ﴾ (it will relate), meaning: it will relate to the creation (تُحَدِّثُ الخَلْقَ),

﴿its news﴾ (﴿أخْبارَها﴾). The first of the two objects has been omitted, because the intended point is the mention of its relating the news, not the mention of the creation. It was said: God will make it speak, and it will inform of what was done upon it of good and evil. And in a hadith: "It will bear witness for every one of them to what they did upon its back."
﴿Because your Lord has inspired it﴾. That is: it reports its news because of your Lord's inspiring it, i.e., to it, and His commanding it to report.

﴿On that Day, people will issue forth﴾: they will come forth from their graves, their places of emergence, to the place of standing (al-Mawqif),

﴿in scattered groups﴾: the white-faced, secure, and the black-faced, terrified. Or they will depart from the place of standing in scattered groups, as the two paths, that of Paradise and that of the Fire, separate them.

﴿That they may be shown their deeds﴾: that is, the recompense for their deeds.

﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good﴾: "dharrah" (a tiny ant), 

﴿good﴾: a specification (tamyiz).

﴿will see it﴾: that is, will see its reward.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 99, verse 8:

﴿And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.﴾ It is said: this is about the disbelievers, and the first (verse) is about the believers. And it is related that a Bedouin (a‘rabi) placed "khayran yarahu" (good, he will see it) out of its order, so it was said to him: "You have put first and put last," and he said:

Take the belly of Harshā, or its back, for indeed
Both sides of Harshā have a path for them.

And it is related that the grandfather of al-Farazdaq came to the Prophet (ﷺ) to have him recite (the Qur'an), so he (the Prophet) recited this verse to him. He said: "Enough for me, enough for me." And it is the most comprehensive verse in judgment, and it is named "al-Jami'a" (the All-Encompassing).
